o: Low Ca, high phosphate, normal ALP, high PTH
Low Ca, low phosphate, low ALP, low PTH
High Ca, low phosphate, low ALP, high PTH
Low (or normal) Ca, low phosphate, high ALP, high PTH
questions.e: Nutritional (vitamin D deficient) rickets: secondary hyperparathyroidism lowers phosphate, ALP rises. Low 25-OH vitamin D.

questions.q: A child has 1 month of polydipsia, polyuria and weight loss. Which will NOT be seen?
questions.e: New-onset T1DM/DKA gives metabolic acidosis with Kussmaul breathing, hyperglycemia and dehydration.

questions.q: A 12-month-old was well until 9 months, when he was weaned to regular foods. Now has FTT, poor appetite, abdominal distension, diarrhea and irritability. Most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Symptoms starting after gluten introduction = celiac disease. CF usually presents from birth.

questions.q: After a minor sliding accident, a child has right-sided pain, abdominal distension on the right, high BP and hematuria. Most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Minor trauma often reveals an existing Wilms tumor (flank mass, hematuria, hypertension from renin).

questions.q: A child has staring, motionless episodes 2-3 times per week preceded by epigastric sensations. Diagnosis?
questions.e: An aura (epigastric rising sensation) means focal onset (often temporal lobe). Focal impaired-awareness seizures last longer than absences, with post-ictal confusion.

questions.q: A boy's growth chart shows short stature with delayed bone age. Most likely diagnosis among these?
questions.e: Delayed bone age: GH deficiency, hypothyroidism, constitutional delay. Normal bone age: familial short stature, skeletal dysplasia. Turner occurs in girls.

questions.q: A boy has palpable purpura on the lower limbs and buttocks, joint pain and abdominal pain. Which immunoglobulin is involved?
questions.e: Henoch-Schonlein purpura (IgA vasculitis). Monitor urinalysis and BP for nephritis.

questions.q: A neglected child in hospital develops pedal edema, ascites, hepatomegaly, and is apathetic and hard to console. Most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Protein-energy malnutrition with edema, fatty liver (hepatomegaly), skin/hair changes and apathy = kwashiorkor.

questions.q: A 2-day-old term neonate has multiple firm yellow-white 1-2 mm papules with a surrounding erythematous flare on the trunk. Wright stain shows many eosinophils. Active and feeding well. Diagnosis?
questions.e: Erythema toxicum neonatorum: benign, eosinophil-filled pustules with red flare, days 1-3. Transient pustular melanosis has neutrophils and no erythema.

questions.q: An 18-month-old boy: what can he do?
o: Stands on one leg for 10 seconds
questions.e: A doctor's note in the PDF says "help to undress" is right, but two copies of the key highlight "copies line". Kept the doctor's answer. By standard milestones, 18 months removes clothes; imitating a stroke/line is about 2 years.

questions.q: A girl has migratory arthritis after a GAS infection. What is true about this arthritis?
o: It affects large and small joints
questions.e: Rheumatic fever arthritis: very painful, migratory, large joints, responds dramatically to aspirin, leaves no deformity.

questions.q: A 14-year-old with asthma on a bronchodilator exercises normally, has no night waking, and had one ER-treated exacerbation last year. State of his asthma control?
questions.e: Control is judged on the last 4 weeks of symptoms (daytime symptoms, night waking, reliever use, activity limitation). A past exacerbation is a future-risk factor, not a control criterion.

questions.q: An 18-month-old has a brief generalized seizure with fever 40 C. During a (normal) LP he passes a large watery stool with blood and mucus. Most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Shigella: high fever, febrile seizures (neurotoxin), bloody mucoid diarrhea.

questions.q: A 9-month-old has a bulging fontanelle and head circumference above the 98th percentile, with suspected hydrocephalus. Next step?
questions.e: Imaging to define the cause and ventricles (cranial US is possible while the fontanelle is open; MRI is ideal). Diuretics are not a treatment.

questions.q: A 6-day-old with birth weight 3000 g now weighs 2950 g. Next step?
questions.e: A 1.7% loss at day 6 is well within normal physiological weight loss.

questions.q: A 3-year-old (born at 36 weeks, RDS, bronchiolitis last winter) has recurrent cough and shortness of breath triggered by colds, dust and cold weather. His brother has similar symptoms. He has allergic shiners and nasal congestion; lungs are clear. Which best predicts future asthma?
o: Wheezing triggered by cold weather and dust
questions.e: Official key: allergic shiners, a sign of allergic rhinitis/atopy, which is a predictor in the asthma predictive index. Sibling asthma and prematurity are not API criteria.

questions.q: Which primitive reflex is present at birth and disappears by 6 months?
questions.e: Official key: Moro. Moro disappears by about 4-6 months. Timings for the other reflexes vary by source, so learn Moro for this question.

questions.q: A 6-year-old ingested many aspirin tablets a few hours ago. He is lethargic with a respiratory rate of 30. Best initial management?
questions.e: Official key: activated charcoal (salicylates are well adsorbed, and charcoal is useful even several hours after ingestion). Protect the airway first in a lethargic child. Bicarbonate for urine alkalinization follows.

questions.q: A girl with type 1 diabetes has 3 days of fever, diarrhea and vomiting. She looks well hydrated, fasting glucose is 260 mg/dL, bicarbonate is normal and urine shows ketones. After adjusting the insulin dose, what is the next step?
o: Tell her to measure urine ketones daily
Tell her to measure blood glucose daily
Tell her to increase her hydration
questions.e: Official key: admission. Ongoing vomiting with ketosis in T1DM risks rapid progression to DKA, and she cannot keep up oral intake. Sick-day monitoring at home is every 2-4 hours, not daily.

questions.q: An 8 kg child with moderate dehydration has sodium 155. Which maintenance fluid and rate is correct?
questions.e: Official key: D5 0.45% saline at 32 mL/h. Rate = 4 mL/kg/h x 8 kg = 32 mL/h. Hypernatremic deficit is then replaced slowly over 48 h.
